chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr: from one who asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mosque whose qiblah wall seeps from a drain in which urine is passed.
So he said: “If its seepage is from the drain, then do not perform salat (prayer) in it; but if it is from other than that, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.الْبَالُوعَةِ: the drain or sewage pit from which impurity may seep
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque being asked about as the place of salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَائِطُ قِبْلَتِهِ: the wall facing the qiblah in the mosque
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a mosque whose wall is seeping from a drain?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning performing salat (prayer) in a mosque whose qiblah wall has moisture or seepage. If the seepage comes from a foul drain, prayer there is prohibited; if it comes from another source, then there is no objection.
